_comment: Structured release notes embedded into the GameCTL binary and served at GET /api/release-notes. Human companion: /CHANGELOG.md (keep in sync). 'version' matches the build stamp from -X main.version (a git tag like v0.0.2-beta, or a short commit SHA for untagged builds). The 'unreleased: true' entry is shown for any running build whose version does not match a tagged entry.

releases.name: v0.0.43-beta
releases.summary: Three games could be deployed onto a port nothing was listening on, and it looked like nothing was wrong. When GameCTL moved a server to a free port, the port moved but the game didn't — so the server ran perfectly while being unreachable, with no error anywhere. Also: one failed update could keep a server down indefinitely, and Palworld joins the catalog.

changes.title: A failed update no longer keeps a server down forever
changes.detail: The CS2 init container ran steamcmd under set -e and only wrote its “already handled this request” marker after it succeeded. So when an update failed, the marker was never written, the next start saw the same request as new, and it re-ran the identical failing update. Seen in the wild: one forced validate hit a stale Steam appmanifest and latched the server into a crashloop for roughly ten hours and 119 restarts — while the game itself was fully installed and perfectly playable the entire time. None of it was visible in the UI, because a pod's main containers do not start until its init containers finish, so the log pane simply stayed empty. A failed update now warns and starts the server on the existing install, and the request is recorded either way — the marker means “we acted on this”, not “it worked”. A failed first install still stops, since there is no game to fall back to.

changes.title: Servers deployed on a reassigned port are reachable again
changes.detail: GameCTL recommends a different port when the one you picked is already claimed, and both the Service and ProxyCTL's forwarding follow that choice. Barotrauma and Necesse never told the game about it, so the game stayed on its default port while everything around it moved. The result is a server that starts cleanly, reports itself healthy, and cannot be connected to by anyone — with nothing in any log to explain it, because from the server's point of view nothing failed. Barotrauma was found running on 27015 behind a forward for 27022. Both now pass the chosen port through to the server itself. Project Zomboid had the same latent problem and is fixed in its image.

changes.title: Barotrauma can be listed in the public server browser
changes.detail: Three separate faults stacked, and each one hid the next. Its image silently overwrote the query port with the game port on every boot, which is harmless while a server is private but makes it fail to start the moment it is made public. Once that was fixed, the game port and the forwarded port disagreed. Once that was fixed, the query port — the one the in-game browser actually probes — was reachable in-cluster but not from outside. Finally, the server's outbound registration left via the cluster's home connection while its public ports lived on the proxy, so the master server advertised an address with nothing listening on it. Barotrauma now publishes in egress mode, the same as IW4X and Wreckfest 2, so the address the master server records is the one players can reach.

changes.title: Palworld
changes.detail: Deploy a Palworld dedicated server from the wizard, with the game installing to its volume on first boot rather than into the image, so moving the server between nodes does not re-download it. Both UDP ports are wired up from the start — the game port and the separate Steam query port — because forwarding only the game port is what leaves a server joinable by direct IP but invisible in the browser. Palworld is the heaviest server in the catalog; the default resource profile reflects that, with a ceiling chosen to keep a 16 GB node schedulable for anything else.

releases.name: v0.0.42-beta
releases.summary: A Factorio server could be bricked permanently by a single storage or network blip. One partial autosave was enough to make it fail on every boot, forever, while a perfectly good save sat next to it. It now cleans up after itself.

changes.title: A partial autosave can no longer brick a Factorio server
changes.detail: Factorio autosaves by writing <name>.tmp.zip and then renaming it over <name>.zip — atomic only if the rename happens. Interrupt the write (a storage hiccup, a network blip on NFS-backed saves, the pod killed mid-save) and a truncated .tmp.zip is left behind. Because the server starts with --start-server-load-latest it then loads that file, being the newest in saves/, and dies with "Opening zip .../world.tmp.zip failed: I/O error" on every boot from then on — until someone notices and deletes it by hand, with a complete save and five valid autosaves sitting right beside it. GameCTL now moves any partial autosave aside before the server starts. It is moved, not deleted, so the bytes remain if one is ever worth recovering, and load-latest is kept because picking the newest autosave is the right thing to do after a real crash. Existing servers get this on their next deploy from the wizard.

releases.name: v0.0.41-beta
releases.summary: IW4X gets a real map rotation you can build, save and apply without it being erased or reverted, plus a fix for the Bot Warfare pathfinding that froze servers for 25 seconds at a time. Also fixes a crash that made the Monitoring page unusable.

changes.title: IW4X map rotation you can actually manage
changes.detail: Set the rotation in the deploy wizard, then edit it live from the server's control panel. A saved rotation now survives a restart instead of reverting to the image default, Save / Apply / Restart do what their names say, and changing map by hand no longer gets stomped by the rotation on the next cycle. Applying a rotation also stopped erasing the one you had just built.

changes.title: IW4X map changes apply the game type too
changes.detail: Change map sent the map without the game type, so the server loaded the new map under whatever mode it was already running. The map change is now sent first, then the game type, with a pause between them — sending both at once had the server drop one. Gameplay settings are likewise applied after boot, which is the only point they stick.

changes.title: Bot Warfare no longer freezes IW4X servers for 25 seconds
changes.detail: The bundled Bot Warfare mod's A* pathfinding could stall the server thread for around 25 seconds at a time — long enough for every player to time out. The image now patches the pathfinder so bot navigation stays inside a sane budget.

changes.title: The Monitoring page white-screened on every visit
changes.detail: The metrics-server card rendered before its status request had resolved and read a field off a null response, which threw and took the entire page down — Monitoring was unreachable rather than merely missing a panel. It now renders immediately with the install command and fills in the specifics once the status arrives.

changes.title: The metrics-server command sits at the top of Monitoring
changes.detail: Retitled to "Can't see CPU/RAM metrics? Run this" and moved to the top of the page. CPU and RAM graphs are the reason to open Monitoring, so the command that makes them work belongs where you land — not underneath the panels that are empty precisely because it hasn't been run.

changes.title: CarX Drift Online and Assetto Corsa
changes.detail: Both were catalog entries that never reached a working deploy, so they are gone rather than sitting in the picker as dead ends. The IW4X map list was corrected at the same time.

releases.name: v0.0.40-beta
releases.summary: Two new games: IW4X (Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 2) and DayZ. IW4X runs on GameCTL's own iw4x-kube image — a Wine runtime that downloads nothing, validates the game files you supply, and fails with the missing filename instead of sleeping forever like the abandoned community image it replaces. It comes with a live control panel: roster, map and gametype switching, bot management, kicks, editable bot names, and an admin list for the in-game bot menu. DayZ brings back the shared Steam account page, since its server can't be downloaded anonymously. Plus the DEV BUILD badge works again — it had been silently hiding itself on every dev build since the first release tag.

changes.title: IW4X (Modern Warfare 2) servers
changes.detail: Deploy an IW4X dedicated server from the wizard. IW4X is Windows-only, so it runs under Wine in GameCTL's own iw4x-kube image (published at ghcr.io/gamectl-hq/iw4x-kube). You supply the game directory — your own legally owned MW2 install with IW4x installed into it — and the Storage step prints the exact rsync/kubectl commands with your host and path already filled in. The image never downloads game content and never sleeps on failure: a missing iw4x.exe or main/iw_00.iwd is reported by name and the pod exits, so a server that cannot work never reports itself Running and Ready. DLC is optional; base-map-only installs are normal.

changes.title: IW4X live controls on the manage screen
changes.detail: A panel alongside the CS2 and Wreckfest ones: the live roster with scores, pings and a BOT badge, per-player kick, map and gametype switching, map restart, a say box, and bot fill/spawn. Bot names are editable — per row or as a list — and are written to the file IW4x reads at startup, so the panel tells you a restart is needed rather than pretending the change is live. An admin section grants Bot Warfare's in-game menu (Action Slot 2) to chosen players, with one-click add from the roster so nobody has to retype a 16-character GUID.

changes.title: RCON for idTech3 games
changes.detail: The RCON console previously spoke only Valve's Source protocol over TCP. IW4X and Quake 3 speak the idTech3 connectionless UDP dialect instead, so their console appeared but every command failed. Both now work, dispatched on the game type, with the console's quick-command buttons filled in for each.

changes.title: DayZ servers
changes.detail: DayZ's dedicated server (Steam app 223350) cannot be downloaded by anonymous SteamCMD — it needs an account that owns the game. The entry wires that to the shared Steam account below, and a missing login stops the pod with a legible reason instead of silently retrying anonymously and dying minutes later on a missing binary. GameCTL writes its own config file rather than fighting the image's, so turning managed config off hands back an untouched file to edit. Shipped deployable but unverified: booting it needs a DayZ-owning account, which only an operator can supply.

changes.title: Steam account settings page (restored)
changes.detail: One shared Steam login for games SteamCMD can't fetch anonymously, stored as a write-only Secret in your cluster and referenced by deployments through secretKeyRef — never written into a manifest and never shown again after saving. Removed last May when nothing used it; DayZ uses it again.

changes.title: The DEV BUILD badge stopped hiding on dev builds
changes.detail: The badge decided whether a build was a release with an unanchored version match. That worked while the repository had no tags, because the version stamp was a bare commit SHA. From the first release tag onward every dev build stamped something like v0.0.39-beta-2-g6b89f15-dirty, whose leading v0.0.39 matched — so the badge vanished exactly when it mattered, and a build running uncommitted code presented itself as a tagged release. It now requires a complete version, so a commit-count suffix or a dirty tree correctly reads as a dev build.

changes.title: Steps can title their own file-seeding instructions
changes.detail: The wizard's copy-paste panel for operator-supplied files had SPT/Fika's wording hardcoded, so any other game needing seeded files got instructions about Fika mods. Games can now supply their own title and explanation; IW4X uses it for MW2 game files.

releases.name: v0.0.39-beta
releases.summary: The deploy wizard now knows which ports the rest of your cluster is already using — it names the server that holds one, recommends free ones you can click, and stops the Build button rather than letting a collision through. Publishing through ProxyCTL no longer dead-ends when a public port is taken; it republishes on a free one and still delivers to the port your server actually listens on. Plus Factorio finally honours the ports you pick, gains a LAN/public visibility toggle, and a CS2 install-time crash loop is fixed.

changes.title: The deploy wizard knows what ports are already in use
changes.detail: Port fields were generated blind: nothing told you the 27015 you typed is already CS2's RCON port, and the collision only surfaced later as a broken server or a rejected publish. Every port field is now checked against a live inventory of every Service port in the cluster. It names whoever holds the number, and offers the nearest free ports as one-click chips. The check is graded rather than absolute, because two ClusterIP Services legitimately share a number: sharing is a warning that needs an explicit acknowledgement, while the same port and protocol on the same LoadBalancer IP is a hard error with no override. Build YAML stays disabled until one or the other is satisfied, and the acknowledgement is tied to the exact conflict it was given for — change a port and it drops, so a "yes, I know" can never be carried onto a collision you never saw. Applied across every game's port fields.

changes.title: Factorio: choose who can find and join
changes.detail: A visibility toggle picks between Open/LAN (unlisted, no factorio.com account required on either end) and Public (listed on the factorio.com server browser, with player verification on). Public authenticates with either a token or your account password, whichever you have. The setting is re-applied on every restart, so switching later is a redeploy rather than a hand-edit on the volume.

changes.title: Publishing through ProxyCTL no longer dead-ends on a taken public port
changes.detail: ProxyCTL routes one public port to exactly one target, so publishing a second game on a Source-default port failed with "27015/udp is already routed by enabled entry cs2" and stopped there; the deploy's publish phase became something you had to go resolve by hand in another app. ProxyCTL was already returning the nearest free port in that error and already supported a public-to-target remap — GameCTL was discarding both. It now retries on the suggested public port, pinned to deliver to the port the game actually listens on, so nothing about the game server changes and only the number players type moves. Each remap is reported in the task log.

changes.title: Factorio honours the ports you choose
changes.detail: The generator emitted RCON_PORT but never PORT, so changing the game port renamed the container and Service ports while the server carried on listening on 34197. RCON had no wizard field at all, pinning it to 27015 no matter what CS2 or Project Zomboid already held. Both are now wired through, RCON is editable, and it defaults to 27016. Factorio settings the wizard owns are also re-applied on every start now; previously the image seeded its config only on first boot, so changing one of them on an existing server silently did nothing forever.

changes.title: CS2 servers no longer crash-loop on install
changes.detail: The install init container ran under a login shell. As PID 1 that made bash source ~/.bash_logout on exit, which on Debian-based images calls clear_console; that fails in a container, and with set -e still in effect the failure replaced the script's own successful exit. The pod sat in Init:CrashLoopBackOff having logged nothing but its success message. Triggered in the wild when the upstream SteamCMD image picked up a base carrying that .bash_logout.

changes.title: Heartbeat strips span the full window
changes.detail: The strip anchored its left edge to the oldest sample on hand, so bars grew in from the left and the bar count itself climbed for the first ~20 minutes of history — bars multiplying and narrowing on every refresh, with each card rendering a different-length strip. It now always spans the requested window, with empty buckets in grey, so a young history reads honestly as "1h, partly filled".

changes.title: Heartbeat strips fill their container
changes.detail: A short history rendered as a few huge slabs in a left-aligned stub, sitting above full-width CPU/RAM lines at about a third their width. Bars now flex to fill, so fewer buckets simply render wider.

changes.title: "What's new" no longer shows an empty "Unreleased" section
changes.detail: Any build whose version didn't match a tag — that is, every dev build between releases, which is what you are most likely running — was shown a placeholder that told it nothing. It now falls back to the newest released entry.

changes.title: The metrics-server install command is always on the Monitoring settings page
changes.detail: It used to appear only once GameCTL had decided something was wrong, which is not when you go looking for it.

releases.name: v0.0.38-beta
releases.summary: Restart no longer hangs on servers that were deployed before GameCTL pinned the Recreate rollout strategy — with one-click repair for the ones you already have. Resource and memory fields become stepped controls instead of free text, so a mistyped quantity can't silently resize a server. Plus working metrics-server detection, heartbeat uptime graphs throughout, and safer instance naming.

changes.title: Restart no longer deadlocks on single-replica game servers
changes.detail: Eight generators (Barotrauma, Core Keeper, Factorio, Necesse, Project Zomboid, Quake 3, Terraria, Valheim) emitted no rollout strategy, so Kubernetes defaulted to RollingUpdate and scheduled the replacement pod BEFORE terminating the old one. The new pod had to find a second copy of the CPU and RAM the running server still held — on a cluster without that headroom it stayed Pending forever and Restart looked hung. Both pods also mounted the same save data during the overlap, and on a ReadWriteOnce volume the new pod could not attach at all. Those generators now emit strategy: Recreate, and the apply-time normalizer enforces it for every single-replica, volume-backed Deployment so a redeploy repairs older instances too.

changes.title: One-click repair for servers deployed before that fix
changes.detail: Restart only patches the pod template, so it keeps whatever strategy a Deployment already has — meaning existing servers were not fixed by restarting them, and nothing repaired them implicitly. GameCTL now detects instances still on RollingUpdate and offers to fix them from the game hub (all at once) or from a single server's manage screen. The change is non-disruptive: the rollout strategy lives outside the pod template, so nothing restarts — it only changes what the NEXT restart does. Switching an existing Deployment also required clearing the API server's defaulted rollingUpdate block first, which server-side apply cannot express; GameCTL now does that with a merge patch.

changes.title: metrics-server detection works on a stock install
changes.detail: The check inspected the metrics-server Deployment in kube-system and the metrics.k8s.io APIService — neither of which GameCTL's namespace-confined RBAC permits — so on every stock install it failed with a permission error the UI swallowed, and no CPU/RAM guidance ever appeared. It now performs the same namespaced metrics read the sampler already relies on, so it works with the permissions GameCTL ships with, and distinguishes "cannot determine" from "not installed" rather than nagging when it simply cannot tell.

changes.title: metrics-server is installed by you, not by GameCTL
changes.detail: The in-app "Install metrics-server" button applied cluster-scoped RBAC, an APIService, and a kube-system Deployment from inside the pod — work GameCTL's ServiceAccount is deliberately not allowed to do, so the button could only ever fail with a permission error. It is replaced by the exact kubectl command to run, with a copy button, shown only when metrics genuinely are unavailable. GameCTL's permissions stay as narrow as they were.

changes.title: CPU and memory are stepped controls, not free text
changes.detail: Kubernetes quantities are easy to get wrong in ways the API accepts silently: "2G" is two billion bytes rather than 2Gi, and a bare "2" for memory means two BYTES. Both the deploy wizard's Resources step and the manage screen's resource editor now use plus/minus steppers — CPU in millicores, memory in half-Gi increments — that emit a valid quantity every time and show what the value means in plain language. The manage screen's controls are also much larger and refuse to apply a request that exceeds its limit.

changes.title: Minecraft's JVM heap is a stepper too
changes.detail: The Memory field is written straight into the server's MEMORY setting and the container's requests and limits are derived from it (heap minus 1Gi, heap plus 1Gi). Its parser silently falls back to the 4G default on anything it cannot read, so "4 GB" or "4gb" quietly gave you a different heap AND different container resources with no error. It is now a whole-GB stepper that always emits the expected form, and shows the container limit it implies as you change it.

changes.title: Instance names are assigned, and identity fields are locked
changes.detail: GameCTL deploys every game into a single namespace, so a duplicate server name did not error — it overwrote the running instance and shared its storage folder. The wizard now assigns the next free name automatically (valheim, then valheim-2, valheim-3) and makes the server name and namespace read-only, with a guard that renames and asks you to rebuild if a name is taken between opening the wizard and deploying.

changes.title: Only supported games appear in the deploy picker
changes.detail: The picker previously offered everything in the catalog minus a per-game "coming soon" flag, so a generator added to the repo became deployable by default and a forgotten flag was invisible to the operator. Deployable games are now an explicit allowlist: a new game is not offered until it has been deployed and verified. The games available today are unchanged.

changes.title: Storage paths tolerate a trailing or doubled slash
changes.detail: A Storage Location typed as "/mnt/ssd/" was rejected with "path is not normalized", which never mentioned the trailing slash that caused it, and the preview rendered the game's data path with a doubled slash. Paths are now normalized (whitespace, repeated and trailing slashes) before validation on the server and as you type in the UI, while directory traversal is still rejected rather than silently rewritten. This also fixes the installer's storage-location option failing when its path ended in a slash.

changes.title: Uptime is shown as a heartbeat graph everywhere
changes.detail: The manage screen drew uptime as a latency line with unreachable samples plotted as 0ms, which rendered an outage as an impossibly fast response instead of an absence. Every uptime view now uses the same heartbeat bars — one bar per time bucket, green when all checks in it passed — with latency as its own line built only from samples that actually answered. Hovering a bar raises it and shows that bucket's time range and result, the graphs carry visible start and end times, and the hub cards state the window they cover.

changes.title: Requests wait longer before giving up
changes.detail: The UI's request timeout was 15 seconds. Several endpoints talk to the Kubernetes API before answering, and a busy cluster could exceed that — surfacing as a bare "Network Error" on a request that had in fact succeeded. It is now 30 seconds: long enough to ride out a slow API server, short enough that a genuinely dead backend still reports quickly.

releases.name: v0.0.33-beta
releases.summary: Wreckfest 2 joins the roster as GameCTL's first Wine-based game, so Windows-only dedicated servers are now on the table. Plus clearer storage docs and an MIT license.

changes.title: Wreckfest 2 support (first Wine-based game)
changes.detail: Full wizard support for Wreckfest 2 on GameCTL's own from-scratch image (ghcr.io/gamectl-hq/wreckfest2-kube). The WF2 dedicated server is Windows-only, so it runs under WineHQ stable with a virtual display — the first game in the fleet to do so, and the pattern future Windows-only servers will follow. The wizard covers the server browser name, welcome message, join password, event rotation, lobby countdown and vote times, admin flags, and the game port (default 30100 UDP). Like the rest of the fleet the ~2GB server installs to your volume on first boot and normal boots never run SteamCMD.

changes.title: Clearer storage prerequisites in the README
changes.detail: Documents that importing existing game files as any user is supported, and that the images self-heal ownership on boot — so you do not have to chown a save directory by hand before pointing GameCTL at it.

changes.title: MIT license
changes.detail: GameCTL now ships a LICENSE file (MIT), so the project is explicitly free to use, fork and self-host.

releases.name: v0.0.32-beta
releases.summary: GameCTL now pairs with ProxyCTL end to end: pick an "Internet" mode in the deploy wizard and your server — and its companion sites like BlueMap or CS2 surf records — get their public DNS as part of the deploy itself. Deleting a server can clean all of that up again.

changes.title: Publish servers on the internet from GameCTL (ProxyCTL integration)
changes.detail: Every server card gains a Networking panel showing both exposure paths side by side: the LAN (MetalLB) address and the public (ProxyCTL) one. Link a sibling ProxyCTL install once (URL + its operator login, verified against its API and stored in a Secret); after that, publishing is subdomain + domain + one click — GameCTL creates the tunnel entry targeting the game Service's live ClusterIP and triggers ProxyCTL's apply, DNS included when ProxyCTL has a Cloudflare token. Pause/resume, re-apply, and unpublish live in the same panel, and if a redeploy moves the Service's ClusterIP the panel flags the drift with a one-click re-point.

changes.title: All-in-one deploy: DNS association happens at apply time
changes.detail: The wizard's Networking step gains a Player access choice (LAN / LAN + Internet / Internet only) plus a public subdomain — pre-filled with your server name — and a domain dropdown fed from your linked ProxyCTL. The choice rides the manifest as annotations, and right after a successful apply the deploy task runs a 'Publish via ProxyCTL' phase that mints every hostname. Services get ClusterIPs at apply time, so there is no waiting on pods, and the phase runs server-side — closing the browser doesn't matter. Best-effort: a publish failure marks the phase in the task log, never the deploy.

changes.title: Multi-Service instances publish per target
changes.detail: Instances with more than one bindable Service — Minecraft + BlueMap, CS2 + its surf-records site — get one publish row per target with role chips (game / bluemap / records), each binding its own subdomain and ports. Auto-publish names companions <subdomain>-<role>.<domain>.

changes.title: Web companions ride ProxyCTL's Cloudflare Tunnel
changes.detail: HTTP targets (BlueMap, surf records) publish as ProxyCTL web routes instead of raw L4 ports: cloudflared in-cluster → Cloudflare's edge, TLS and WAF included, no droplet port consumed. The panel shows the https:// address with an open-in-tab link.

changes.title: Delete optionally removes public access too
changes.detail: The delete confirmation gains an 'Also remove ProxyCTL public access' checkbox (on by default). The delete task unpublishes first — tunnel entries, web routes, and their DNS records — while the Services the bindings resolve through still exist, then sweeps the cluster. A failed unpublish never blocks the delete.

changes.title: RCON ports are never published
changes.detail: Game Services carry an rcon port for GameCTL's own console, reached internally via ClusterIP. The publish port derivation excludes rcon-named ports, so a publish can't put RCON on the public internet — an exposed RCON port gets brute-force-scanned within hours.

changes.title: Internet-only mode skips MetalLB entirely
changes.detail: With 'Internet only' selected the generated Service stays ClusterIP — ProxyCTL's in-cluster gateway reaches it directly — so a public-only server doesn't consume a LAN IP, and every MetalLB pool/IP field in the wizard (including BlueMap's) hides when it doesn't apply.

changes.title: Minecraft's BlueMap download EULA defaults to accepted
changes.detail: Deploying through the wizard already accepts the Mojang EULA (EULA=TRUE), and BlueMap's asset-download gate mirrors that same EULA — the old 'No' default just shipped a map whose webserver was silently down. The opt-out remains.

changes.title: Released builds hide the 'Unreleased' notes section
changes.detail: The in-app What's-new list only shows the Unreleased staging entry on dev/SHA builds; tagged releases list exactly what shipped.

releases.name: v0.0.31-beta
releases.summary: Fixes game-server creation failing against NFSv3-only servers (common on NAS defaults) with a misleading 'Couldn't reach NFS server' error.

changes.title: Game-server creation works on NFSv3-only NFS servers
changes.detail: The NFS helper pods mounted exports without 'nolock', so on servers that only speak NFSv3, mount.nfs tried to launch rpc.statd through a wrapper that calls GNU 'flock -e' — an option BusyBox's flock doesn't have. statd died, the mount failed with exit 32, and the UI blamed it on 'Couldn't reach NFS server'. The helper pods only create, inspect, and delete directories — NFS file locking buys them nothing — so they now mount with 'nolock' and skip statd entirely. NFSv4 servers ignore the option, so nothing changes for them.

releases.name: v0.0.30-beta
releases.summary: GameCTL updates only when you ask. It pins itself to a fixed version, so a pod restart can no longer bump you to a new build unprompted.

changes.title: GameCTL no longer updates itself without prompting
changes.detail: Installs now pin an immutable version tag instead of a moving ':latest'. Previously the deployment re-pulled the newest published image on any restart, so an ordinary pod reschedule — a node drain, an eviction, or re-running the installer — could silently upgrade GameCTL to a build you never chose. Now a restart re-pulls the exact same version, and the only thing that moves you to a new release is clicking 'Update'.

changes.title: 'Update' pins the specific new release
changes.detail: The in-app update button used to just restart the deployment and let it grab whatever ':latest' pointed at. It now sets the container image to the exact release tag it's offering, so you land on precisely that version — and stay on it across restarts until you choose to update again.

releases.name: v0.0.29-beta
releases.summary: Game servers now deploy on NAS boxes that only speak NFSv3 — GameCTL lets the mount negotiate its NFS version instead of demanding v4.2.

changes.title: NFS storage works with servers that don't speak NFSv4.2
changes.detail: GameCTL previously pinned every NFS mount to version 4.2. On a NAS that only offers NFSv3 (common on older Synology/QNAP units, or anywhere v4 is disabled) the mount silently failed and the game pod hung before it ever started — surfacing as an unexplained deploy timeout rather than a storage error. Mounts now leave the version unset so the client negotiates the best version both ends support (4.2, 4.1, 4.0 or 3). This affects every game's generated storage as well as the internal helper that creates and cleans up NFS directories. If your server already speaks 4.2 nothing changes.

releases.name: v0.0.28-beta
releases.summary: Save-file backups (schedule, retention, restore) — now rock-solid to list and easy to inspect — plus reliability polish: Valheim starts cleanly on the first deploy, and new NFS shares get a guided setup.

changes.title: Save-file backups with schedule, retention and restore
changes.detail: Each game's Manage screen now has a Backups panel: pick a destination storage location (e.g. a roomy HDD share), an interval (hourly / 6h / daily / weekly or a custom cron) and how many backups to keep, and GameCTL runs a CronJob that snapshots just the save files and rotates out the oldest. 'Back up now' takes an on-demand snapshot and 'Restore' stops the server, restores a chosen archive, and starts it again — both tracked in the Tasks menu. Backups know each game's real save paths (e.g. Satisfactory SaveGames, Factorio saves, Core Keeper worlds), so they skip multi-GB game installs; a whole-volume option is available per game, and match servers with no save (CS2, Quake, L4D2) are flagged as having nothing to back up.

changes.title: Stored backups now list reliably, even on clusters without internet
changes.detail: The Backups panel could show 'No backups yet' even when archives existed on the share. Listing now mounts the destination the same way backups are written (an inline NFS volume) instead of an in-pod mount that needed the node to reach the internet — so your archives show up everywhere.

changes.title: Valheim starts reliably on the first deploy
changes.detail: The Valheim image's SteamCMD occasionally fails its very first download with 'Failed to install app 896660 (Missing configuration)', leaving the pod stuck on the initial step (worst on slower hosts). GameCTL now primes and pre-downloads the server with retries before the image's own updater runs, so it comes up on the first try — and world saves stay on your persistent storage.

changes.title: Guided NFS share setup and a backup-archive how-to
changes.detail: The Storage Locations screen has a 'How to make an NFS Share? (Ubuntu)' walkthrough with copy-paste apt commands, plus a reminder that the export must let the cluster mount it (export to * or list your node / pod network). The Backups panel now shows how to open a .tar.gz archive (tar -tzvf to peek inside, tar -xzf to extract) and the exact on-share path where the files live.

changes.title: Thanks to Grizz for troubleshooting Valheim
changes.detail: A tip of the hat to Grizz for the hands-on help tracking down the Valheim first-boot SteamCMD failure.

releases.name: v0.0.21-beta
releases.summary: CS2 now reliably updates to the latest build on every (re)start — no more getting stuck on an old build that clients can't join — and surf's !replay / !ghostcam plus the speed/timer HUD finally ship (the embedded plugin had drifted behind its source). RTV gains more surf maps and admin map/mode pickers.

changes.title: CS2 reliably updates to the latest build (no more SteamCMD "0x6" stuck updates)
changes.detail: On the kus image a freshly-downloaded SteamCMD would self-update mid-run and leave the game update wedged at state 0x6, so the server silently launched a STALE build and players on the newer client build couldn't connect. The boot now pre-warms SteamCMD and clears stale staging before updating, so the latest build always lands. The manage-screen 'Auto-update on next start' toggle works for CS2 again (full validate vs fast start).

changes.title: Surf !replay / !ghostcam and the speed/timer HUD now actually ship
changes.detail: The surf HUD plugin (base64-embedded in the generator) had drifted behind its source, so deployed servers ran an old build missing the recent !replay / !ghostcam (chicken/hostage/cube ghost models + fading trail) and timer/HUD work. The plugin is rebuilt and re-embedded; a new deploy gate + CI check stop a stale plugin from silently shipping again.

changes.title: RTV: more surf maps, admin !modes / !maps pickers, and a changelevel-freeze fix
changes.detail: Five more surf maps were added to the in-game !rtv pool, plus admin !modes / !maps pickers. GameCtlRtv is now the sole map/mode handler (the kus image's own Map/Mode commands are disabled), fixing a freeze where a typo'd !map name made the image announce a changelevel that then failed and hung everyone.

changes.title: CS2 wizard welcome-message example is now generic
changes.detail: The first-install welcome-message placeholder no longer contains a personal server name.

releases.name: v0.0.20-beta
releases.summary: Surf servers now spawn players weaponless (knife only) instead of with the default pistol — surf is a movement game, not a gunfight. Reminder: a working surf server with the SharpTimer timer must be DEPLOYED as surf through the wizard; the live-panel Surf button only switches cvars and cannot install the plugin stack.

changes.title: Surf servers no longer spawn players with a pistol
changes.detail: The surf cfg profile now empties the default primary/secondary loadouts so players spawn with a knife only, disables the buy menu and money, gives free armor, and enables instant respawn (a missed ramp shouldn't bench you for a round). Surf is a pure movement mode — the starting pistol was leftover from CS2's Custom-mode defaults. This applies to servers deployed as surf via the wizard.

changes.title: Reminder: surf timer requires a wizard surf DEPLOY, not a live mode switch
changes.detail: The SharpTimer plugin stack (timer, zones, speed HUD, records) is installed by an init container that only exists on a server deployed as surf through the wizard. Clicking the live-panel 'Surf' button on a non-surf server switches game_type/cvars over RCON for the movement physics, but cannot install plugins — so there's no timer or speed display. To get the full surf experience, deploy (or re-deploy) the CS2 server with the 'Surf (timer + records)' wizard mode selected.

releases.name: v0.0.19-beta
releases.summary: CS2 gets a Surf game mode with the full SharpTimer plugin stack (timer, zones, records), Steam Workshop map support, and one-click game-mode switch buttons on the manage screen. Also fixes a long-standing bug where the CS2 live panel always showed the wrong current mode.

changes.title: CS2 Surf mode — SharpTimer plugin stack, auto-installed
changes.detail: The CS2 wizard has a new 'Surf (timer + records)' game mode. Picking it runs the server as game_type 3 / game_mode 0 (Custom) with surf movement cvars (sv_airaccelerate 800, bunnyhop, no fall damage, endless rounds) written into the operator-owned gamemode cfg, and adds an init container that installs the full CS2 surf plugin stack onto the data volume: Metamod:Source, CounterStrikeSharp (pinned to a SharpTimer-compatible build), the SharpTimer timer/zones/records plugin, plus MovementUnlocker and RampBugFix. The init container patches gameinfo.gi for the Metamod search path, is idempotent (a version-marker file gates re-downloads), and re-applies the gameinfo.gi patch every boot since a CS2 update overwrites that file. SharpTimer records and config persist on the data volume across redeploys. Note: on a brand-new data volume the gameinfo.gi patch lands on the second boot (CS2 isn't installed yet when init containers first run); deploying surf onto an existing CS2 data path works on the first boot.

changes.title: CS2 Steam Workshop maps
changes.detail: The CS2 wizard now has Workshop map fields — a single map's numeric Workshop ID or a whole collection's ID — wired to the image's CS2_HOST_WORKSHOP_MAP / CS2_HOST_WORKSHOP_COLLECTION env vars. Surf maps (and KZ, bhop, etc.) are all Workshop content, so this is required for a surf deploy. On the manage screen the live Map panel grew a 'Workshop map ID' input that loads any workshop map on the running server via host_workshop_map.

changes.title: One-click game-mode switch buttons on the CS2 manage screen
changes.detail: The CS2 live panel now has a row of one-click mode buttons (Competitive, Casual, Wingman, Demolition, Deathmatch, Arms Race, Surf) alongside the existing dropdown — click one to switch the running server to that mode immediately (current bot difficulty + player cap kept), with the active mode highlighted. Switching to Surf on a server that wasn't deployed as surf applies the movement physics but not the timer plugin (the plugin stack only installs on a real surf deploy).

changes.title: CS2 live panel showed the wrong current game mode
changes.detail: The backend read un-prefixed env names (GAMETYPE / GAMEMODE / MAXPLAYERS / SRCDS_ADDITIONAL_ARGS) that the joedwards32/cs2 image never receives — the generator emits CS2_*-prefixed names. So the manage screen's CS2 panel always fell back to 'Competitive' and a 16-player cap regardless of the server's actual mode, and bot difficulty was misread. The backend now reads the correct CS2_GAMETYPE / CS2_GAMEMODE / CS2_MAXPLAYERS / CS2_BOT_DIFFICULTY vars, plus a new CS2_GAMEMODE_PROFILE discriminator so Surf (which shares game_type/game_mode with a raw Custom server) is reported correctly.

releases.name: v0.0.18-beta
releases.summary: Fixes the silent 'copy address' and 'copy password' buttons on plain-HTTP installs, and beefs up the visual confirmation so you can see the copy succeeded.

changes.title: Copy buttons (IP address, credentials) now work over plain HTTP
changes.detail: The browser's `navigator.clipboard.writeText` API only exists in secure contexts (HTTPS or localhost). GameCTL is commonly accessed over plain `http://lan-ip:8080`, where the API is undefined — so `navigator.clipboard?.writeText(...)` short-circuited to undefined, the `.then()` that set `copied=true` never ran, and the click was a silent no-op with no feedback. There's now a `copyText()` helper that tries the modern API first and falls back to a hidden-textarea + `document.execCommand('copy')` trick that works on every modern browser, including non-secure contexts. The CopyableAddress chip and the CredentialRow copy button both use it.

changes.title: Copy buttons show an obvious '✓ Copied!' confirmation
changes.detail: Successful copies now color-swap the whole chip/button (emerald background + bigger '✓ Copied!' label) for ~1.5 seconds instead of a faint grey tick. Failed copies (e.g. when no clipboard API is available at all) color-swap to a rose ✗ with a hint to select manually, so the click is never a silent no-op.

releases.name: v0.0.17-beta
releases.summary: Fixes the nonsense update banner that read 'GameCTL v0.0.15-beta is available — you're on v0.0.16-beta', and surfaces the Storage Test as a five-step plan so you can see exactly what the probe checks (mount → mkdir → write → read → delete) with a check/X next to each step in the result.

changes.title: Update banner no longer claims an older release is 'available'
changes.detail: The update checker compared versions with `!=` (inequality) instead of a proper semver 'b > a' check, so any brief window where the GitHub Releases API still pointed at the previous release (a normal lag between `git push --tag` and the release workflow marking the new Release as 'latest') would trip the banner with the wrong direction — 'v0.0.15-beta is available — you're on v0.0.16-beta'. The checker now parses both sides as semver (with prerelease handling, so v1.0.0-beta < v1.0.0) and only sets updateAvailable=true when latest is strictly newer than the running build. Unparseable inputs (SHA-stamped dev builds, empty strings, 'dev') never flip the banner.

changes.title: Storage Test button now shows the five-step plan + per-stage outcomes
changes.detail: The Test button result panel now renders the probe's checklist — Mount the share / Create the .gamectl-probe test directory / Write a small test file / Read it back and verify the bytes / Delete the test file — with a green check next to each step that ran successfully and a red ✗ on the failing one (subsequent steps are shown as 'not reached'). While the probe pod is running the same list is shown with a pulsing indicator so you can see what the test is actually doing. The backend's StorageProbeResult now includes a `steps` array driving this; existing fields (`ok`, `stage`, `message`, `hint`, `details`) are unchanged.

releases.name: v0.0.16-beta
releases.summary: Storage Locations now has a Test button per row that actually verifies reachability + read/write before you deploy a game against it. Spawns a one-shot probe pod that mounts the share the same way a real game would, writes + reads + deletes a tiny test file, and classifies any failure with a targeted hint (server unreachable, export not granted to this node, read-only export, root_squash, etc.) — no more 'the deploy looked fine until the pod tried to write'.

changes.title: Storage Locations: Test reachability + read/write per row
changes.detail: Each location row in Storage Locations now has a 'Test reachability + read/write' button. Clicking it spawns a short-lived probe pod in the gamectl namespace that mounts the same inline NFS (or hostPath) volume a real game would use, then in order: mkdir's the .gamectl-probe subdir under the configured top-level folder, writes a tiny test file, reads it back and compares bytes, deletes the file, and exits. The UI shows a green '✓ Mount + read/write OK · <ms>' on success and a red strip with the failing stage + a targeted hint on failure. The probe pod is always deleted on the way out and has a 20s hard deadline. New endpoint: POST /api/storage/locations/test.

changes.title: Targeted error classifier for storage test failures
changes.detail: Failures don't just print the raw kubelet message — the backend classifies them by stage so the hint matches the actual cause. Examples: 'mount' stage 'access denied' → 'The NFS server refused the mount. Add the node's IP to /etc/exports and run exportfs -ra'; 'mount' stage 'no route to host' → 'NFS server unreachable from the node, check port 2049/TCP'; 'mkdir' stage → 'Read-only export or root_squash + wrong uid; mark the export rw (consider no_root_squash)'; 'write' stage → 'Read-only export or filesystem out of space'; 'timeout' stage → falls back to the mount classifier with the kubelet's waiting message in the details. The raw output is always available under a 'raw output' details twirldown for the cases where the classifier guessed wrong.

releases.name: v0.0.15-beta
releases.summary: Closes the loop on the install flow — the bootstrap token in the URL printed by install.sh now actually pre-fills the first-run setup field. The installer side has been printing `?token=…` for several releases, but the UI half (reading the param and seeding the form) was missing in the published build, so operators were copy/pasting the token by hand even though the URL already carried it. Please update.

changes.title: First-run setup: bootstrap token from `?token=…` actually pre-fills the field
changes.detail: install.sh prints the first-run URL with the bootstrap token in the query string (`http://host:8080/?token=abc…`), so the operator only needs a username + password. The UI side of that — reading the param and seeding the setup form — was missing from the published image: the field initialized as an empty string and the token had to be pasted by hand. Now the bootstrap field is initialized from `URLSearchParams(location.search).get('token')` on first render, and on a successful setup POST the token query param is removed from the URL via `history.replaceState` so a refresh doesn't re-attempt with the now-dead token.

releases.name: v0.0.14-beta
releases.summary: Finishes the k3s fresh-install path the previous two releases started — please update. v0.0.13's kubeconfig-perm fix copied the file to ~/.kube/config, but the k3s-wrapped kubectl (a symlink to the `k3s` binary) **hardcodes** /etc/rancher/k3s/k3s.yaml unless $KUBECONFIG is set, so the installer still aborted on the retry. The installer now also exports KUBECONFIG for the current run and appends it to ~/.bashrc for future shells.

changes.title: Installer now sets $KUBECONFIG so the k3s kubectl wrapper actually uses ~/.kube/config
changes.detail: On k3s, `kubectl` is typically a symlink to the `k3s` binary (`k3s kubectl`), and that wrapper hardcodes /etc/rancher/k3s/k3s.yaml unless $KUBECONFIG is set in the environment. So v0.0.13-beta's copy to ~/.kube/config wasn't enough by itself — the wrapper kept trying the root-only file and the installer aborted on the second cluster-reachability check. The installer now does both halves of the fix: copies the kubeconfig (if not already done) AND exports KUBECONFIG=$HOME/.kube/config for the rest of its run, and appends the same export to ~/.bashrc so future shells work without manual setup. The detection block also now handles the 'partial fix from a previous run' state (file already at ~/.kube/config) by re-using it instead of re-prompting.

releases.name: v0.0.13-beta
releases.summary: Follow-on hotfix to v0.0.12-beta — the installer now handles the second-most-common first-install footgun on a fresh k3s box: kubectl refusing to talk to the cluster because /etc/rancher/k3s/k3s.yaml is root-only. The installer detects this and offers to copy the kubeconfig to ~/.kube/config (y/N). Also clarified in the README that GameCTL is tested on k3s.

changes.title: Installer auto-fixes the k3s kubeconfig-permission failure
changes.detail: On a fresh k3s install, /etc/rancher/k3s/k3s.yaml is owned root:root mode 600 by default, so `kubectl` as a normal user gets 'permission denied' on the kubeconfig and the installer aborts with 'kubectl can't reach a cluster.' The installer now detects this specific shape (k3s present, no KUBECONFIG set, no ~/.kube/config, not running as root) and offers a y/N prompt to copy the kubeconfig to ~/.kube/config owned by the current user (mode 0600). On 'no', it prints the exact one-liner to run by hand. Decline-and-retry behavior is non-destructive — nothing is touched without consent.

changes.title: README: 'Tested on k3s' note added to the install section
changes.detail: GameCTL targets any conformant Kubernetes 1.28+, but the installer's bootstrap helpers (auto-detected ingress, optional MetalLB install, k3s kubeconfig-permission fix) are shaped around k3s — the easiest path from 'blank Linux box' to 'running GameCTL'. Other distros (microk8s, kubeadm, EKS/GKE/AKS, kind) work too; the note in the README is now explicit about that scope.

releases.name: v0.0.12-beta
releases.summary: Hotfix release — please update. The `curl | bash` installer was aborting on a fresh shell before it could deploy anything (BASH_SOURCE unbound under set -u), so new k3s installs were blocked. Also a full Terraria fix: swapped to a maintained vanilla image, killed the startup-crash NPE, and bumped default CPU so Large worlds actually finish generating. Plus a CS2 hibernate-when-empty wizard toggle.

changes.title: Installer no longer aborts under `curl | bash`
changes.detail: Running `curl -fsSL https://gamectl.cc/install.sh | bash` on a fresh machine failed before doing any work with `BASH_SOURCE[0]: unbound variable` / `cd: null directory`. When the script is piped from stdin there's no file on disk, so `BASH_SOURCE[0]` is unset, and combined with `set -u` the SCRIPT_DIR resolution aborted. The installer now defaults BASH_SOURCE[0] to empty, skips the cd when no source file exists, and falls through to fetching the manifest from the published URL — the intended path for `curl | bash`.

changes.title: Terraria: server actually starts and is playable end-to-end
changes.detail: Three bugs were stacked. (1) The `mark2dot0/tshock` image was last updated in 2021 and is pinned to Terraria 1.4.2.3, so current 1.4.5.x clients connected, the TCP handshake completed, then the protocol handshake silently failed — the client hung forever at 'Found Server'. The wizard now defaults to `ryshe/terraria:vanilla-1.4.5.6` (actively maintained, matches current retail Terraria, no TShock account/login dance). (2) `TerrariaServer.exe` spawns an input-reader thread (`startDedInputCallBack`) that NPEs on a null Console stream when stdin isn't attached — the container now sets `stdin: true` and `tty: true` so the dedicated server boots instead of crashlooping. (3) World gen is single-threaded; the previous 1-core CPU limit made Large worlds take 20+ minutes. Defaults are now `cpu: 500m / 2`, surfaced as editable fields in the wizard form.

changes.title: CS2 wizard: 'Hibernate when empty' toggle (default on)
changes.detail: CS2's `sv_hibernate_when_empty 1` keeps an empty server idle (no map tick) so it doesn't burn CPU during off-hours. Exposed as a wizard checkbox, on by default. Turn it off if you want a server that stays warmed up — e.g. for a quick-join workflow where the first connector shouldn't wait the few seconds for the map to wake.

releases.name: v0.0.11-beta
releases.summary: CS2 is finally playable end-to-end (5v5 vs bots, RCON, no 65G re-download); Minecraft gets a full live-controls panel; explicit Restart / Stop / Start on every instance card; auto-update toggle no longer restarts the server.

changes.title: CS2: 5v5 vs bots actually plays now (movement, weapons, bot fill)
changes.detail: A stack of related bugs left freshly-deployed CS2 servers with one frozen bot, players who connected but couldn't move or switch weapons, and instant 'Going to intermission…' loops. Root causes fixed together: the generator emitted env vars the joedwards32/cs2 image does not read (HOSTNAME/RCON_PASSWORD/GAMETYPE/SRCDS_ADDITIONAL_ARGS — now CS2_SERVERNAME/CS2_RCONPW/CS2_GAMETYPE/CS2_ADDITIONAL_ARGS); CS2 regenerates gamemode_<mode>.cfg from the depot on every boot, wiping the image's bot sed (now overridden by an operator-owned gamemode_<mode>_server.cfg written by an init container, with mode-pinned mp_maxrounds, mp_roundtime, mp_freezetime, mp_halftime, mp_match_can_clinch, mp_autoteambalance/limitteams so Casual↔Competitive panel switches can't strand the server in a Game-Over latch); CS2's match-start team-intro cinematic and competitive's online-warmup hold (mp_team_intro_time / mp_warmup_online_enabled) — both froze players in place on a community/bot server — are disabled in that override.

changes.title: CS2 wizard no longer re-downloads the full ~65G install on restart
changes.detail: The joedwards32/cs2 image's SteamCMD retry path does `rm -rf $STEAMAPPDIR/steamapps` (deleting the appmanifest) on any non-zero exit; that forces the next attempt to pull the whole game from base. With auto-update on, the heavy ~65G `validate` could trip this on its own (especially OOM-killed under the previous 2Gi memory cap). The wizard now defaults Auto-update to Disabled (the install persists on NFS and is reused for fast starts; first deploys still install fine — SteamCMD always runs), and the cs2 memory limit is bumped 2Gi → 4Gi so validate has headroom when you do enable updates. Default data PVC size 50Gi → 100Gi (the install alone is ~65G).

changes.title: Restart / Stop / Start on every instance card
changes.detail: Each game instance card now has explicit Restart, Stop, and Start controls next to Delete. Restart does a rolling restart (and applies any pending settings — see auto-update below). Stop/Start scale to 0/1 replicas.

changes.title: Auto-update toggle no longer restarts the server when flipped
changes.detail: Toggling the per-instance 'Auto-update on next start' setting used to immediately roll the Deployment. The choice is now recorded as a Deployment metadata annotation (no pod disruption); the live toggle shows an amber 'pending — restart to apply' badge when the saved value differs from the running pod's env. The new Restart button is the single point where the change applies — it folds the pending env into the same rollout.

changes.title: One-click CS2 controls on the manage screen
changes.detail: The CS2 live-controls panel grew a 'Quick actions' row driven by Source RCON: Restart round (mp_restartgame 1), End warmup, Swap teams, Pause/Unpause, Add bot, Kick bots, plus a Change-map dropdown of the standard pool with a one-click Load map. All ride the existing /rcon endpoint — no pod restart for any of them.

changes.title: Full Minecraft live-controls panel on the manage screen
changes.detail: New per-instance panel mirroring the CS2 layout: Difficulty and Default gamemode selects with Apply; World subsection split into Time (Day/Night/Noon/Midnight), Weather (Clear/Rain/Thunder, applied with a long duration so the change visibly sticks), Actions (Save / Save off / Save on / Reload / List), and Whitelist (on / off / reload list); a Gamerule dropdown of 20 boolean gamerules with true / false / query buttons; a Players section with a name input plus Role buttons (OP / De-op / Kick / Ban / Pardon / Whitelist +/−) and per-player Gamemode buttons (Survival / Creative / Adventure / Spectator); and a Broadcast row that pushes a /say message with Enter-to-send. The generic RCON terminal still renders below for anything not on a button.

changes.title: Terraria no longer hangs on the 'Choose World' prompt
changes.detail: The mark2dot0/tshock image ignores the WORLD_*/MAX_PLAYERS env vars the generator was setting, so first-time servers dropped into the interactive world picker and spun forever on EOF. The Deployment now passes real Terraria server CLI args (-world /world/<name>.wld -autocreate <size> -worldname <name> -difficulty <n> -maxplayers <n> -port <n> [-password <pw>]) — the world auto-creates on first boot and loads thereafter.

changes.title: Grey-screen crash on the CS2 manage page (and missing Minecraft RCON console)
changes.detail: The per-game RCON quick-commands code referenced an undefined `game` identifier during render, throwing a ReferenceError that took down the whole manage page on cs2 (grey screen) and silently hid the RCON console + OP buttons on Minecraft. Affected every RCON-capable game (cs2, minecraft, factorio, project-zomboid).

changes.title: Logs and RCON console no longer scroll the whole page on refresh
changes.detail: The log/RCON panels used scrollIntoView() on a sentinel inside the box, which scrolls the nearest scrollable ancestor up to and including the document — so every 5-second log auto-refresh yanked the page down to keep the log in view, pulling buttons out from under the operator. Both now scroll only their inner container. The log viewer also stops auto-following the tail the moment you scroll up to read older lines, and resumes tailing when you scroll back to the bottom.

changes.title: RCON now finds the password regardless of image convention
changes.detail: Backend RCON only looked for an env var named RCON_PASSWORD, but the CS2_* env mapping fix renamed it to CS2_RCONPW (the joedwards32/cs2 image's actual name) — so the CS2 Live panel and RCON console reported 'server has no RCON_PASSWORD set' even though the password was right there. The lookup now recognizes RCON_PASSWORD and CS2_RCONPW (and falls back across the known list).

changes.title: CS2 wizard: GSLT field clarified with a steamgamesettings.com link
changes.detail: The SRCDS Token (GSLT) wizard field now has a placeholder and hint explaining what a token gives you (persistent server identity, public server-browser listing, VAC-eligible) and links to steamgamesettings.com for app ID 730. The server runs and is joinable by direct connect without one — it's not strictly required, just recommended for an internet-facing server.

changes.title: CS2: removed the 'Pin to node (hostname)' field
changes.detail: CS2 was the only game exposing a nodeSelector — a generic, empty-by-default convenience from the original wizard with no resource or hostPath reason to keep it. It has been removed from both the wizard schema and the generated Deployment spec.

changes.title: CS2: map picker is now a dropdown and uses the correct env var
changes.detail: The free-text 'Map' field is replaced with a 'Start map' dropdown of common maps (de_dust2, de_mirage, de_inferno, de_nuke, de_overpass, de_vertigo, de_ancient, de_anubis, de_train, cs_office, cs_italy) plus a 'Custom / workshop map…' option that reveals a free-text field for off-list or workshop maps. The selection is now wired to CS2_STARTMAP (with CS2_MAPGROUP=mg_active), the env vars the joedwards32/cs2 image actually reads — the previous MAP env var was never honored by the image, so the configured map had no effect.

changes.title: Minecraft: BlueMap webroot consolidated onto the main data volume
changes.detail: When BlueMap is enabled, GameCTL no longer provisions a separate PV/PVC (and its own storage path) for the web tiles. The webroot lives under the main Minecraft data volume, so the extra volume was redundant. The redundant PersistentVolume, PersistentVolumeClaim, pod volume and volume mount are removed; tiles now persist on the existing data PVC and remain regenerable from the world. The BlueMap Service and plugin install are still gated by the BlueMap toggle — only the storage backing changed. Migration: for a server whose tiles currently live on the old separate path, re-applying the manifests drops the old binding and BlueMap re-renders into the data volume on next start (no data loss — the world is the source of truth). To skip the re-render, copy the existing tiles into the data volume's bluemap/web directory before re-applying; the old path and its PV can be removed once the new render is confirmed.

releases.name: v0.0.10-beta
releases.summary: Satisfactory storage fix (persistent install + saves) and per-game SteamCMD update controls.

changes.title: Satisfactory install & saves now persist (production bug)
changes.detail: The Satisfactory data PVC mounted at /srv/satisfactory, but the wolveix/satisfactory-server image installs the ~4.5GB game files, saves and backups under /config. The persistent volume held nothing useful, so every pod restart re-downloaded the whole game via SteamCMD (often crash-looping on exit code 8) and lost all saves. The data volume now mounts at /config, so installs and saves survive restarts and upgrades — no more multi-GB re-download or lost worlds.

changes.title: Per-game SteamCMD update controls for Satisfactory
changes.detail: New wizard options replace the old inert 'Run update on start' field (the image never read RUN_UPDATE_ON_START/INSTALL_IF_MISSING). 'Update via SteamCMD on every start' (off by default) reuses a populated /config volume for fast starts; 'Force a one-time SteamCMD update on next deploy' runs a single validate/update and stamps a gamectl.io/steamcmd-update pod annotation so the Deployment actually rolls. Both drive the SKIPUPDATE env var the wolveix image actually reads.

changes.title: In-app release notes
changes.detail: The update tool now shows what each GameCTL build changes, with per-fix bullets keyed to the running and available version.
